title: Spot the Flaw: Integration Review
brief: Two teams modelled the claims domain separately and someone merged the files the night before a review. The merge parses, loads and looks plausible on the canvas — which is the problem. Four faults survived it: a table nobody wired in, a foreign key pointing at a name that was refactored away, a pair of tables that reference each other in a loop, and a reference code whose format rule cannot fit the column it is declared on. That last one is real history: it is the contradiction that produced this appliance's PATTERN_EXCEEDS_LENGTH check, after a synthetic-data generator was asked to satisfy a VARCHAR(6) column and an eight-character pattern at the same time and could only choose which constraint to break. Find all four and re-validate.

entities.description: An insurance policy as sold, one row per policy version.

columns.name: policy_reference
columns.description: Business reference printed on the policy document.

columns.name: product_sk
columns.description: The product this policy was sold under.

entities.description: The insurance products available to sell.

columns.name: flagship_policy_sk
columns.description: The policy the other team used as this product's exemplar.

entities.grain: One row per claim submitted against a policy.

columns.name: policy_contract_sk
columns.description: The policy this claim was raised against.

columns.name: adjuster_grade
columns.description: Seniority grade used to route complex claims.

expected_flaws.hint: Count the characters the pattern on policy_reference demands, then read the column's declared length.
expected_flaws.fix: The pattern needs eight characters (AAA-1234) and the column allows six, so no value can satisfy both. Widen the column to VARCHAR(8) if the format is genuinely required — and if the requirements never stated that format, delete the pattern instead. A guessed format ships as a contract term your customer's data is tested against.

expected_flaws.hint: Every table named on the right of a relationship should also be on the canvas.
expected_flaws.fix: The claims team wrote its foreign key against dim_policy_contract, a name the other team refactored to dim_policy. Repoint the relationship at dim_policy.policy_sk. Nothing warns you at load time: the reference is only wrong relative to a table that is not there.

expected_flaws.hint: One table has no line drawn to it at all.
expected_flaws.fix: dim_adjuster arrived with the merge and was never joined to anything. Either relate it to fact_claim through an adjuster foreign key on the fact, or remove it — an unreachable dimension is either a missing join or dead weight, and both are decisions worth making deliberately.

expected_flaws.hint: Follow the arrows from dim_policy and see where you end up.
expected_flaws.fix: dim_policy points at dim_product, and dim_product points back at dim_policy through flagship_policy_sk. There is no order in which these two tables can be loaded. Break the loop: the flagship policy is an attribute of the product's marketing, not a structural dependency, so drop that foreign key or move the association to a separate bridge table.

solution_notes:
The lesson is that a merged model can be syntactically perfect and structurally impossible. Three of these four faults are invisible in any single file — they exist only in the relationships between files, which is exactly what a review of merged work has to look at.

On the reference code: this is the appliance's own history. The synthetic-data generator clamps a value it generated to a declared VARCHAR(n), but refuses to clamp one produced from a regex, because truncating that value breaks the pattern it was generated to satisfy. That refusal is correct, and it leaves a contradiction with nowhere to go — the generator can only pick which constraint to violate. The check exists because a generator is the wrong place to discover a modelling error.

Expected end state: the claims relationship repointed at dim_policy, the product-to-policy loop broken, dim_adjuster either joined to fact_claim or removed, and policy_reference either widened to VARCHAR(8) or stripped of a pattern nobody asked for. Re-validate and the model is clean.
